title: Talent Acquisition Specialist (5-Month Maternity Cover Contract)
description:

Founded in 2006, CXG is a global customer experience company uniquely positioned at the intersection of data-driven retail performance, customer experience transformation, and operational execution across 200+ luxury brands worldwide.
The mission of our 270 collaborators is to help brands transform customer and employee experiences through tailored insights, strategy, and implementation.
We are passionate about delivering impact.
Your role:
As a Talent Acquisition Specialist, you will be part of CXG ’s Global People Team, reporting directly to the Chief People Officer. Throughout this maternity cover, you will lead end-to-end recruitment across CXG ’s offices worldwide, supporting our global growth by attracting and hiring the best talent. You will also oversee global mobility processes and contribute to People initiatives that enhance employee experience and operational effectiveness.

• Lead global mobility processes, including geographical relocations and departmental/internal moves.

• 4+ years of experience in Talent Acquisition within an international or fast-paced environment.

• Strong interviewing and assessment skills.

• Experience with ATS platforms, assessment tools, and HR systems (e.g. Factorial and other AI recruitment tools).

• Ability to operate autonomously with high ownership, make informed decisions, and drive processes end-to-end without daily oversight.

• Strong sense of prioritization and ability to handle simultaneous global searches under tight deadlines.

description:
Our Why At Dotmatics 

At Dotmatics, a Siemens company,  we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. Our Portfolio includes Luma, LumaLab Connect, ELN Platform, Graphpad Prism, Geneious, SnapGene, Protein Metrics, OMIQ, FCS Express, LabArchives, NQuery, EasyPanel, SoftGenetics and Virscidian.

We have a vision for a new Lab of the Future that will change the future of scientific research.

We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform - best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. This is not flat data buried away in digital graveyards. This is dynamic, multi-dimensional decision-making.

Scientific enterprises need a new level of effectiveness to achieve tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Illness will not wait. The biosphere will not wait. We are tireless in our vision, because the time for innovation is now.

Shaping the Future of Science At Dotmatics 

Our global team of more than 800 colleagues are dedicated to supporting our customers in over 180 countries. Together, with our scientific community of users, we accelerate scientific innovation in order to make the world a healthier, cleaner, and safer place to live.

You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation.  Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.

We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together. 

What do we need 

We are looking for an experienced market leader, thought leader and SME in Lab Automation and Orchestration.
Lab automation is where science meets engineering. Robotics, liquid handlers, instruments, and scheduling software are moving labs from manual work toward automated, data driven, and eventually autonomous operation. While we are supporting fully automated labs, most labs still run as islands. Instruments speak different languages, workflows are hard to change, and the data that comes off the line rarely arrives ready for analysis or AI. 

We’re building Luma, a Scientific Intelligence Platform for life sciences and materials science. Lab Orchestration and automation are core to our Molecule to Market story, and they connect directly to the strengths of Siemens in industrial automation. We need someone to own the market strategy for it.

This is a customer and market facing role. You’ll spend real time with lab automation leaders at pharma, biotech, CDMOs, and research institutes across the UK and Europe, hearing what they need and bringing it back to the business. You’ll also support teams around the world across Siemens, including sales, product, services, customer success, and the Siemens Solution Marketing team, so everyone can speak to the lab automation market with confidence and one consistent story. You’ll work with industry thought leaders to shape the conversation on autonomous labs and AI. Your job is to drive software adoption and AI use cases in lab automation. You will shape where we play, who we sell to, how we position, and how we win.

• Market analysis: sizing segments, tracking competitors and automation vendors, and spotting trends early

title: Senior Data Analyst, Reliability Assessment
description:
Our Company

The North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) is a not-for-profit international regulatory authority whose mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid. NERC develops and enforces Reliability Standards; annually assesses seasonal and long‐term reliability; monitors the bulk power system through system awareness; and educates, trains, and certifies industry personnel. NERC’s area of responsibility spans the continental United States, Canada, and the northern portion of Baja California, Mexico. NERC is the Electric Reliability Organization (ERO) for North America, subject to oversight by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and provincial authorities in Canada. NERC’s jurisdiction includes users, owners, and operators of the bulk power system, which serves nearly 400 million people.

Our Mission

The vision for the ERO Enterprise, which is comprised of NERC and the six Regional Entities, is a highly reliable and secure North American bulk power system. Our mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid.

Your Impact

The Senior Data Analyst, Reliability Assessment, applies technical skill, experience, and subject-matter expertise in the areas of data management and analysis to support the ERO’s efforts to independently assess and report on the overall reliability, adequacy, and associated risks to the interconnected North American bulk power system. This Senior Data Analyst role includes responsibilities to collect, process, and analyze data necessary for assessing risks that could arise from the growing reliance on natural gas for electricity generation, with application to resource adequacy and bulk power system reliability assessments.

The Senior Data Analyst is part of the reliability assessment team that provides superior technical analysis and designs ERO processes for developing and publishing NERC’s reliability assessment reports, including the Long-Term Reliability Assessment and seasonal assessments. The Senior Data Analyst coordinates with the Performance Analysis team to provide reliability assessment information and analysis for the State of Reliability report and the Data and Analytics Integration team on data management, data quality, and analysis.

The Senior Data Analyst, Reliability Assessment, reports to the Manager, Reliability Assessments.

Your Role

• Working with members of the reliability assessment team, analyze and interpret energy supply and infrastructure information, including: electricity generation, load, and transmission system data; and natural gas supply and infrastructure data.

• Develop data requests and manage timely collection of reliability data from NERC registered entities to support the identification of electric reliability risks in NERC reliability assessments, with a focus on risks related to interdependent electric-natural gas energy systems.

• Develop, implement and manage approaches, methods, and processes to promote data quality and reduce potential for data errors following best practices on data management.

• Support the transformation of complex data into visualizations for use in NERC reliability assessments products.

• Collaborate with NERC and ERO Enterprise subject matter experts that manage and use various reliability data systems on projects to make systems more compatible and interoperable.

• Make use of available datasets containing generation, load, transmission, and natural gas fuel supply information to augment NERC’s collected data in analyzing trends and emerging risks to electric reliability.

• Proactively identify and suggest solutions to technical analysis and data problems.

• Develop working knowledge of the fundamentals of NERC Reliability Assessments.

title: Analyst
description:
The Role
As our Analyst, you'll be the analytical engine behind our online sales and paid acquisition. You'll track how every channel performs, find where we're winning or wasting spend, and give marketing, merchandising, and leadership clear recommendations. The role suits someone equally comfortable in a spreadsheet, a SQL editor, and a conversation with a media buyer.
Compensation : Indian Rupee $70,000 - $100,000 montly
What You'll Do

• Own reporting on ecommerce performance (traffic, conversion rate, AOV, revenue, margin) and paid media (ROAS, CAC, CPA, CTR, CPM) across Google, Meta, TikTok, Amazon Ads, affiliates, and other channels.

• Build and maintain dashboards in [Looker Studio / Tableau / Power BI] that give teams a single source of truth.

• Analyze campaign and channel performance, and recommend budget allocation and bid, audience, and creative optimizations.

• Design, run, and read A/B tests on landing pages, site experience, promotions, and ad creative.

• Evaluate attribution across channels using platform data, GA4, and incrementality or MMM approaches where available.

• Analyze customer behavior, including cohorts, retention, lifetime value (LTV), repeat purchase rates, and LTV:CAC by channel.

• Support merchandising and promotional planning with product, category, pricing, and discount performance analysis.

• Forecast revenue and marketing spend for weekly, monthly, and seasonal peaks such as Black Friday/Cyber Monday and holidays.

• Audit tracking and data quality (pixels, UTMs, conversion APIs, GA4 events) with marketing and engineering.

• Present findings to non-technical stakeholders with clear, actionable recommendations.

What You Bring

• 2-4 years of experience in ecommerce, digital marketing, or retail analytics.

• Strong SQL skills and advanced Excel/Google Sheets.

• Hands-on experience with GA4 and at least two major ad platforms (Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, TikTok Ads, Amazon Advertising).

• Experience building dashboards in a BI tool.

• Solid grasp of performance marketing metrics, funnel analysis, and attribution concepts.

• Working knowledge of A/B testing and basic statistics (significance, sample size).

• The ability to explain complex data simply and turn analysis into a clear "here's what we should do."

• Attention to detail and a healthy skepticism about data quality.

Nice to Have

• Python or R for analysis or automation.

• Experience with Shopify, Magento/Adobe Commerce, or Salesforce Commerce Cloud.

• Familiarity with marketing mix modeling, incrementality testing, or tools like Northbeam, Triple Whale, or Rockerbox.

• Experience with CRM and email/SMS platforms (Klaviyo, Braze, Attentive).

• Experience with data warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake) and dbt.

We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X .

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a fully remote position and we're considering candidates in Germany.

About Product Management

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own the experience for your product as well as its roadmap and competitive positioning, and you will collaborate with company leadership on setting your product's goals. You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.

Product Managers are the bridge that connects R&D to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

The role

As the Staff Product Manager for Enterprise Deployment Solutions, you'll own the Grafana Labs offerings that run outside our standard multi-tenant SaaS. That includes Grafana Federal Cloud , for organizations that need FedRAMP-authorized observability: US federal agencies; state, local, and education (SLED) customers; and commercial companies that sell FedRAMP offerings of their own. It also includes Grafana Cloud Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) , which delivers the full Grafana Cloud experience while the customer pays the infrastructure bill directly to their cloud provider, saving them significantly at scale.

Your mission is to make Grafana Labs the obvious choice for organizations that can't use standard SaaS because of compliance, data, or cost-at-scale constraints. Deployment choices change the product: features that are simple in standard SaaS can be hard, expensive, or impossible in a regulated or customer-owned environment. You’ll be responsible for adapting existing Grafana Cloud capabilities to these environments, deciding which features come in, which wait, and which stay out, and occasionally building something specific to BYOC or Federal Cloud. You'll also help shape which deployment models we offer next.

Along the way, you’ll use AI tools daily to speed up research, analyze product signals, and develop positioning, applying strong judgment to the results.

As the Staff Product Manager for Enterprise Deployment Solutions, you will: 

• Define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Grafana Bring Your Own Cloud and Grafana Federal Cloud products, using product data and market research to balance customer value again

Help Shape the Future of AI in Government
What if your years of experience navigating government regulations, evaluating complex cases, or interpreting public-sector policies could help make artificial intelligence more accurate, reliable, and effective?
At Volga Partners , we're bringing experienced government professionals into the next generation of AI development.
We're seeking Government Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) who can apply their professional knowledge, analytical judgment, and industry experience to evaluate and improve advanced AI models.
This isn't a traditional government position, and you won't be processing applications or managing government caseloads. Instead, you'll use your expertise to assess how well AI systems interpret information, apply regulations, reason through complex scenarios, and produce accurate, defensible conclusions.
Your expertise is what matters. AI experience is a plus, not a requirement.
The Opportunity
As a Government SME, you'll serve as a subject matter evaluator, helping assess the quality, accuracy, and reasoning of AI-generated responses across specialized government functions.
You'll examine realistic scenarios, identify errors or gaps in AI-generated conclusions, and provide expert feedback grounded in established regulations, policies, and professional standards.
Your contributions will help improve how AI systems understand and respond to complex public-sector challenges.
Areas of Expertise We're Seeking
We're particularly interested in professionals with substantial knowledge and practical experience in one or more of these areas:
1. Government Policy, Public Records & Regulatory Compliance

• Interpreting federal, state, or local government regulations and policies

• Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), public records, and disclosure requirements

• Privacy compliance, sensitive information protection, and regulatory auditing

• Evaluating complex compliance scenarios and identifying regulatory risks
2. Government Programs, Eligibility & Administrative Decision-Making

• Interpreting government program requirements and eligibility regulations

• Evaluating complex cases, supporting documentation, and administrative determinations

• Identifying inconsistencies, compliance issues, or unsupported decisions

• Applying professional judgment to regulatory and program-specific scenarios
3. Government Procurement, Contracts & Vendor Evaluation

• Federal, state, or local government procurement processes

• Request for Proposal (RFP) analysis and evaluation

• Contracting standards, vendor selection, and procurement compliance

• Developing or applying evaluation criteria, scoring methodologies, and defensible recommendations
You do not need expertise in every area. We're seeking depth of knowledge within your particular specialization.
What You'll Do

• Evaluate AI-generated responses: Review complex government-related scenarios for accuracy, completeness, reasoning, and regulatory alignment.

• Apply expert judgment: Determine whether AI-generated conclusions are appropriate, defensible, and supported by relevant policies or regulations.

• Identify errors and gaps: Recognize inaccurate interpretations, flawed assumptions, missing information, and potential compliance concerns.

• Validate against authoritative sources: Use applicable statutes, regulations, agency guidance, and professional standards to verify findings.

• Develop evaluation benchmarks: Help establish high-quality reference responses, assessment criteria, and examples of sound professional reasoning.

• Provide actionable feedback: Clearly explain your evaluations and recommend improvements to AI-generated content.

• Collaborate on quality: Apply project-specific evaluation guidelines and participate in quality reviews to support consistency and accuracy.

The largest, most demanding enterprises run on Baseten, and they bring exacting requirements for how people, services, and agents access the platform. You'll own the identity and access layer of the Baseten platform: the authorization model, credential systems, and admin experiences that enterprise IT teams use to govern access for organizations like Harvey, HubSpot, and Notion.

You'll design and build Baseten's fine-grained authorization system from the ground up to support the workflows customers depend on today while giving them cleaner, more precise ways to manage access as the platform grows. Authorization at Baseten requires low-latency permission checks at high request volume, consistent contracts and behaviors across the product suite, and strong security guarantees for mission-critical, highly regulated workloads.

- Lead identity and authorization projects from problem definition and technical design through implementation, launch, and iteration.

- Provide technical leadership and mentorship as the team grows.

- Demonstrated end-to-end ownership: you've taken a system from first design through implementation, production rollout, and iteration with users.

- Experience developing and operating multi-tenant systems at scale, where authorization checks sit in the request path and latency and consistency matter.

- Comfort working across the full stack, from product and application code to cloud and Kubernetes infrastructure.

 

NICE TO HAVE

- Experience with Python and Go.

- Experience running an OpenFGA, SpiceDB, or similar deployment in production, beyond a proof of concept.

- Working knowledge of OAuth, OIDC, and SCIM at the protocol level.

BENEFITS

- Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

title: Lead Product Manager
description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara , we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing - and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role
AI is moving off the screen and into physical operations and Samsara is building it. If you want to be a product manager enabling the transformation behind how the real world works, join us.
We connect the vehicles, equipment, sites, and people behind the physical operations that power our economy. Our platform collects more than 30 trillion data points a year from vehicles that travel 99.9% of U.S. roads, and we design our own hardware to capture it. That mix of hardware, real-world data, and AI is why we're building things no one else can. We don't start with a model; we start with the data, embedded hardware, and deep customer understanding that make AI valuable.
And it's working. Samsara crossed $2.1 billion in ARR last quarter, growing 30% year over year, and we've been GAAP profitable for four straight quarters. Adoption of our AI agents has grown 7x since June, and voice agents overtook chat within four weeks of launch. We're just getting started.
This is a remote role is open to candidates residing in the US.
Why the work matters
Physical operations is tough. The work is repetitive, it's hard to hire for, and when something goes wrong, people get hurt. Our customers make thousands of decisions a day about whether people get home safely and whether deliveries and essential services keep running.
How we hire
We hire product managers into Samsara first and match you with the team and problem where you'll have the most impact. Problem spaces evolve consistently here and what's most important is your excitement about what and how Samsara is building.
You'll meet our Product leaders early in the process and your ultimate manager toward the end, so you get a real view of the whole org.
What you'll do

• Spend time in the field with customers, find the problems that matter most, and rally the troops with a strong perspective on what to build next.

• Build with AI every day: prototype, test, ship fast, and keep pushing what the newest models can do.

• Work across hardware, software, and AI teams to ship products customers pay for.

• Own outcomes end to end, measured in customer impact and revenue.

You'll thrive here if

• You've shipped products customers pay for and can show, with numbers, the impact you personally drove.

• You use AI tools daily and get excited when a new model changes what's possible.

• You find your own problems to work on and take full ownership of the outcome.

• You have strong commercial instincts and want to understand how the product gets sold.

• You have conviction and can move a room quickly, but low ego in changing your mind when someone else is right (or more right).

If that sounds like you, let's go.

title: Senior Design Engineer
description:
ABOUT ENODE

The grid was built for predictable, centralised power. Today it's absorbing intermittent supply from grid scale solar and wind, alongside dynamic demand from EVs, heat pumps, and home batteries. The missing piece is software that can connect and orchestrate these devices at scale.

Enode https://enode.com provides the infrastructure layer that makes this possible. Our Connect https://enode.com/connect API gives energy companies a single integration to 1000+ devices across 80+ brands. Our optimisation https://enode.com/optimize tooling gives energy companies the building blocks to manage those devices locally - think smart charging for EVs. Our Flex https://enode.com/flex product turns those connected devices into a flexible, controllable asset for energy companies.

We work with device manufacturers across the energy hardware ecosystem - from EV brands to heat pump and solar inverter producers. Our customers are energy retailers, utilities, and traders building the next generation of energy services. We're backed by Y Combinator, Lowercarbon Capital, and Creandum.

The decisions made now will shape how the energy system gets built. We're looking for people who take ownership, move fast, and care deeply about the role technology can play in the energy transition.

AI IS FUNDAMENTAL TO HOW WE WORK

AI is how a team our size keeps rewiring the way we work, fast enough to match what our mission demands. We look for people who reach for AI as a reflex and who can drop a habit that used to work. People who care about unblocking others, not just about what they ship themselves. If that's not quite how you work yet but it's the direction you're heading, we'd still like to hear from you. We assess this in our interview process, alongside everything else we look at.

THE ROLE

The design team at Enode ships. We’re looking for a Senior Design Engineer who’s as comfortable in a codebase as they are in Figma, and who closes the gap between the two.

You’ll build the interfaces energy retailers and their developers use: the Enode Platform, where they integrate and debug; Link UI, the flow their customers go through when they connect a car or a heat pump; and the website that tells our story. You’ll turn designs into production-ready code, prototype ideas before they become designs, and help look after the design system that keeps all of it consistent.

You’ll report to Daniël, our Head of Design, and join a small, senior design team that works across product and brand. You’ll have real ownership: what you build goes live.

HOW WE WORK

Day to day, each designer works mostly with their own team of engineers, often alongside a product manager. Every Monday, the designers get together to sync and share their work. We team up on projects when it makes sense, and jump on a quick huddle whenever someone wants feedback.

AI is part of how we work every day. We use it to prototype, explore and build our own tools, so a few people can do a lot. But the craft still matters most, so we care just as much about knowing where it falls short. You’ll help shape how we use it as a team.

title: Technical Lead, AI Email App

title: Operation & Maintenance Engineer (Power Plant) - Memphis
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

OPERATION & MAINTENANCE ENGINEER (POWER PLANT)

As an Operation & Maintenance Engineer, you will keep SpaceXSI’s on-site power plant running. The plant supplies power for high-density AI supercomputing facilities in the Memphis and Southaven area, and it has to stay online 24/7.

You will work across gas turbines and generators, balance-of-plant, fuel gas and process/fluid systems, water, compressed and instrument air, HVAC and cooling, and plant electrical systems. The turbine fleet is several different manufacturers. You are expected to be proficient on every type on site, not specialized in one OEM. You will troubleshoot equipment, direct contractors, and use AI to simplify how the plant is operated and maintained. Your schedule flexes, including nights, weekends, holidays, and callouts, so the plant always has engineering coverage. This is a full-time, on-site role in the Memphis region.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Provide operation and maintenance engineering support for the multi-manufacturer gas turbine fleet, generators, balance-of-plant, process and fluid systems, and plant electrical systems, including protection, e-houses, blackstart, and switching.

• Be proficient across all turbine types on site and apply that knowledge to troubleshooting, maintenance, and operating decisions.

• Flex shifts and work hours, including nights, weekends, holidays, and callouts, to maintain 24/7 engineering coverage.

• Troubleshoot trips, alarms, and equipment failures with the shift team and return the plant to service.

• Direct contractors: define the work, set when it is done, and confirm it is completed safely and correctly.

• Use AI to streamline and simplify engineering, operating, and maintenance work.

• Own reliability on assigned systems: bad-actor elimination, root-cause investigations, and corrective actions.

• Write and maintain the engineering plans and procedures the plant is being stood up on, including operating, maintenance, and switching and isolation instructions.

• Manage the critical-parts list so the right parts are identified, stocked, and ready.

• Build and maintain the preventive and predictive maintenance program in the CMMS, including tasks, frequencies, and as-found/as-left records.

• Support outage planning and execution, and support start-up, shutdown, commissioning, and turnover of new generation and balance-of-plant systems.

• Apply SpaceXAI safety standards in the field, including LOTO, NFPA 70E / arc-flash, confined space, and hot work. Stop work when conditions are unsafe.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, or other engineering discipline.

• 3+ years of operation or maintenance engineering experience in a power plant, generating station, or other high-reliability industrial facility.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience with gas turbines from more than one manufacturer, plus balance-of-plant, fuel gas, water, compressed air, and plant electrical systems.

• Willingness to work rotating or flexible shifts, including nights, weekends, holidays, and on-call, to support 24/7 plant coverage.

• Experience using AI tools to streamline or simplify engineering

description:
About the Company:

Industrious is the largest premium workplace-as-a-service provider and home to the highest-rated workplaces in the industry. We celebrate our people as individuals who can accomplish great things when we work together as one team.

To learn more, visit www.industriousoffice.com/careers http://www.industriousoffice.com/careers.

PRICING ANALYST (REVENUE MANAGEMENT)

Industrious is the largest premium flexible workspace company in the world, operating over 250 locations across 10 countries as part of the CBRE portfolio. We design workplaces where teams feel welcomed, supported, and able to do their best work. The same principle guides how we work together as a company.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Right now, the pricing judgment for Industrious's existing North America private office portfolio sits with one person who has built deep expertise in it: knowing which renewals need a bump, which office needs a promotion instead of a price cut, and which market is quietly slipping. That person is moving on to bigger things, and we need someone to step into that seat, formalize what works, and keep roughly 200 price changes a month running accurately, on time, and grounded in real conversations with the General Managers who run our buildings.

This is a Pricing Analyst, Revenue Management role, reporting into the pricing team. You will own business-as-usual pricing execution for the existing North America private office portfolio, with the scope to grow into other products and regions as the team expands.

WHAT MIGHT YOUR DAY LOOK LIKE

You start the morning scanning the pricing dashboard and notice a suite at 1411 Broadway that hasn't sold in weeks, while the identical suite next door is occupied at full list price. The GM has asked for a price cut. You pull the tour and application data, see it's a single-unit problem rather than a market problem, and decide a one-month promotion makes more sense than dropping the list price and setting up a harder renewal conversation down the road.

By mid-morning, you are on the phone with a GM in Nashville, walking through why an entire category of seven-to-nine person offices isn't moving. You ask about tour volume, application quality, and whether the floor plans still fit what people are searching for. You leave the call with a plan, and the GM leaves it feeling like someone actually looked at their building, not just their numbers.

In the afternoon, you work through the week's renewal batch, running each one against the pricing logic the team uses to decide what gets pushed through and what needs a second look. You flag one segment where occupancy has slipped two months running, log it for deeper review, and jot down a note on the decision tree so the next person doesn't have to relearn it from scratch.

You close the day updating the system with the changes you've made, checking your numbers against the portfolio report, and sending a short note to your manager on the one call that needs a decision above your pay grade.

description:
Why Join Zyte ?
At Zyte , we don’t just extract web data-we tackle some of the internet’s trickiest data collection challenges at a massive scale. We’re a globally distributed team of bold, curious problem-solvers dedicated to delivering clean, reliable web data wherever it’s needed.

• We live and breathe data: We unlock access to open web data, helping everyone from scrappy startups to global enterprises power competitive intelligence, analytics, and cutting-edge AI models.

• Truly remote-first: Work from wherever you thrive. With more than 260 Zytans spread across 33 countries, our diversity is our greatest strength.

• Engineering excellence: We love rolling up our sleeves to dig into complex codebases, test out fresh technologies, and push technical limits. If you love creative problem-solving and delivering rock-solid production software, you’ll feel right at home here.

• Thoughtful architecture: We use a clear system design framework to balance functional needs with architectural trade-offs, making sure our decisions are smart and sustainable.

• Fascinating distributed systems: Solve unique engineering problems across custom networking, high-throughput streaming, and large-scale orchestration under real-world constraints.

• Real ownership: Work on a profitable, industry-leading platform that dedicatedly sets aside time and resources for architectural research and long-term feature design.

What Is This Role All About?
When Zyte API fetches web data, it works through a progressive ladder of routes: standard HTTP requests, headless browsers, and, for the toughest sites, Edge-our custom residential network of real physical devices. Edge is our heavy hitter when all else fails. It runs a Rust peer runtime on residential Windows PCs that long-polls our command-and-control service over mTLS gRPC, making fetches look indistinguishable from real human traffic using genuine hardware, residential IPs, and seamless fingerprints.
Our Edge Platform squad manages both the control plane and data plane of this stack. Right now, we’re expanding from Windows into Android devices on mobile networks and self-hosted Linux (with macOS on the horizon). Mobile is where our biggest opportunity lies: websites that block desktop traffic often welcome a real mobile phone on a 4G connection. That’s where you come in! You’ll be the lead engineer making our peer run smoothly and invisibly across every platform-binding Rust to native network stacks and OS APIs via FFI, and turning scattered devices into a well-oiled, observable fleet. We’re a lean, senior team, so you’ll collaborate closely with our Team Lead, Principal Engineer, and the Browser Stack and Antiban squads.
Requirements
What You’ll Be Doing

• Build our cross-platform peer runtime: Take ownership of the Rust peer binary across Windows, Android, Linux (and eventually macOS)-handling process lifecycles, background tasks, networking, automatic updates, and rock-solid stability on unmanaged hardware.

• Bring Edge to mobile platforms: Port our peer to Android using NDK/JNI, navigating foreground services, battery optimizations, and mobile network quirks to integrate real and emulated device farms into our fleet.

• Master the FFI boundary: Integrate the Chromium network stack (Cronet, C++) and browserless HTTP clients into the peer as clean, well-tested Rust libraries with safe runtime contracts.

• Harness hardware signals: Gather deep hardware and OS reconnaissance from the fleet-mapping TCP/TLS/HTTP fingerprints-and share insights with our Browser and Antiban teams so our emulated tiers stay realistic.

• Make the fleet transparent: Build precise per-device metrics around uptime, drop-off rates, bandwidth, and success rates so we can hold ourselves and supply partners accountable.

• Expand edge capabilities: Add peer-level support for new tasks like captcha solving and browser rendering, while keeping the peer securely isolated from untrusted pages and hosts.

ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. title: Principal Software Engineer - Security
description:
WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a Principal Software Engineer - Security, you will help set the technical direction for Radiant's security capabilities across the cloud platform and infrastructure, leading the design and delivery of the systems that underpin them.

You'll work across identity, access control, secrets, network security, platform hardening, auditability, and compliance controls. You'll partner closely with product, infrastructure, SRE, networking, security, and compliance teams, and with customers on their most demanding security requirements.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role focused on making security embedded, scalable, automated, and easy to consume across the platform, through architecture, code, and the standards other teams build on.

 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Set the technical vision and architecture for security systems and platform capabilities, and lead their design and implementation.

- Design and build core security services across IAM, RBAC, workload identity, secrets, encryption and key management, audit logging, network controls, and policy enforcement.

- Translate product, customer, and regulatory requirements into robust architectures, APIs, and technical designs, working closely with the Security Product Manager.

- Drive automation of policy enforcement, configuration hardening, detection, remediation, and software supply chain security.

- Ensure strong tenant isolation and least-privilege access across the control plane and network and data plane.

- Act as a senior technical voice in enterprise customer security reviews, audits, and incident response.

- Raise the security engineering bar across the organisation through mentoring, code review, and technical standards.

 

YOUR PROFILE

- Strong hands-on engineering skills in one or more systems languages such as Go or similar.

- Extensive experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, with significant depth in cloud and network security, IAM, or security infrastructure.

- A track record of technical leadership at staff or principal level, including setting direction across multiple teams and delivering complex, high-stakes systems.

- Deep technical expertise across:

- Identity & access: IAM, RBAC/ABAC, OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, SSO, federation, mTLS, workload and service identity

- Security controls: applied cryptography, encryption at rest and in transit, secrets management, KMS/HSM, key rotation, policy engines

- Infrastructure: Kubernetes internals, containers and runtime isolation, cloud networking, compute, storage

- Security operations: audit logging pipelines, detection engineering, vulnerability management, incident response

- Automation: policy-as-code, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD security, software supply chain (signing, SBOMs, provenance)

- Hands-on experience with technologies such as Vault, OPA/Gatekeeper, SPIFFE/SPIRE, Kubernetes admission control and security tooling, Sigstore, SIEM platforms, cloud KMS, or similar.

- Deep understanding of multi-tenancy, least privilege, zero-trust architecture, threat modelling, and shared-responsibility models.

- Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001, and how they translate into technical controls.

- Able to balance security, performance, reliability, operational complexity, and developer experience.

- Excellent written and verbal communication, including clear design documents and explaining complex trade-offs to technical and non-technical audiences.

 

WHAT YOU BRING

- Security mindset: Think like an attacker and design systems that fail safely, without making them painful to use.

- Engineering excellence: Write and review code that sets the standard for correctness, reliability, and maintainability.

- Architectural judgement: Make sound long-term decisions on systems that are hard to change once built.

- Technical leadership: Influence direction across teams without relying on authority, and grow the engineers around yo

title: Senior Decision Scientist, Partner Excellence
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Relay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years.

Parcel delivery has a quality problem the industry has learned to live with. Parcels go missing between depots. Parcels get marked as delivered and never reach the customer. Most carriers treat a steady rate of loss as a cost of doing business. Relay is building the delivery company where that stops being true.

That is harder for us than for most, because nearly everyone who touches a Relay parcel is an independent partner. We can't manage them into performance. We have to build the standards, the evidence and the product that make doing the job well the natural outcome. Engineering builds the product changes you design.

PARTNER EXCELLENCE HIGHLIGHTS

- You own decision-making, not the model: you decide which signals count, which checks become rules, and whether each fix belongs in product, policy or training. The squad lead acts on your calls.

- Most of a parcel's journey happens between scans. How do you prove a handover happened without making the job slower for the people doing it?

- A delivery is marked complete and the customer says it never came. How do you tell a wrong address from a handover that went wrong, and put the fix where it belongs: product, policy or training?

- Some checks can only answer "can't tell". Which are worth making provable, and which should we stop measuring?

- A whole area, not a slice: you decide what evidence a whole network runs on, and the result is on the street the next morning.

- Analytics at the front, not in support: the squad's roadmap follows the analysis, in a data team of about 30 across analytics, operational research and data science.

THE OPPORTUNITY

As a Senior Decision Scientist, Partner Excellence at Relay, you'll:

- Decide which Partner Excellence problems are real and which only look real, before anyone builds a fix.

- Design how Partner Excellence decides: which signals count, what evidence the network runs on, and what good looks like.

- Tell the squad lead what to change and what to stop, and get a decision.

- Build the thing that decides: data applications, monitors and alerts, not decks, using Claude and agents to ship your own tools.

- Go and look when the data and the street disagree: the sort centre, the van, the shop.

- Get the missing data built, and prove which fixes worked. In a year, the squad can prove every handover in the network.

WE'RE LOOKING FOR CANDIDATES WHO…

- Have owned fraud, risk or trust decisions end to end: turned investigations into rules, standards or interventions, and owned their number, such as the false positive rate you were held to, rather than building the model.

- Have run investigations in fraud, risk, financia

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE SITE

Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1 , its first hyperscale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed that autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, strengthening America’s warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Manufacturing Test Engineer, you will maintain end-to-end ownership of the aircraft’s testing lifecycle on the production line. In this role, you will design, write, and execute critical test procedures-including final Acceptance Test Procedures (ATPs)-to verify flight-readiness, system safety, and sensor performance before the aircraft leaves the factory floor.

You will bridge the gap between design engineering and physical production, translating complex flight and system requirements into repeatable, highly reliable test processes. Beyond executing tests, you will act as a key leader on the floor by training flight-line technicians, troubleshooting complex avionics and electrical failures, and driving continuous improvement to scale our production throughput.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Author Test Procedures: Write, validate, and maintain clear, step-by-step assembly-level and vehicle-level Acceptance Test Procedures (ATPs) and functional test plans to verify safety-of-flight systems on the Fury aircraft.

• Execute Aircraft Testing: Hands-on execution of system-level checkouts, including power-on testing, flight control actuation sweeps, wire harness continuity, sensor calibrations, and integrated avionics testing.

• Troubleshoot Flight Hardware: Diagnose complex electrical, communication, and mechanical integration failures discovered during testing; identify root causes and implement Corrective Actions (CAPA/RCCA).

• Technician Training & Enablement: Train, certify, and support the aircraft technician team on executing test procedures, utilizing specialized aerospace ground support equipment (GSE), and logging results in the Manufacturing Execution System (MES).

• Continuous Improvement: Analyze test data and cycle times to identify bottlenecks on the flight line; continuously optimize ATPs and automated test scripts to reduce test duration without sacrificing quality or safety.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Flight Test, Quality, and Design Engineering teams to feed production test data back into the design loop, facilitating rapid design updates and product enhancements.

• Improve and sustain existing test systems to improve automation, consistency, total cycle time, and test coverage (DfM)

• Develop library of common failure modes with troubleshooting guide/diagrams for fast issue resolution

• Work with Design, Quality and Manufacturing Engineering teams to support customer returns and failure analysis

• Collaborate with design engineers to provide feedback and recommendations for product enhancements based on test outcomes

• Optimize test strategies for efficiency and effectiveness, reducing test time without compromising q

• Keep the visual and quality bar high for member-facing experiences while keeping the system coherent.

• Help designers grow into Design Engineers: share practices for working in code and with AI, pair with them and review their work.

title: Senior Operational Excellence Manager
description:
Job Description

As the Senior Operational Excellence Manager , you will be the architect of efficiency for our Australia and New Zealand markets. Sitting at the intersection of Planning, FSQA, Procurement, and Fulfillment, you will define our Target Operating Model (TOM) and drive the strategic framework that ensures our end-to-end (E2E) supply chain is lean, scalable, and resilient.

This role is based in Chippendale, Sydney and reports to the Associate Director of Operations Enablement .

 

You will…

• Define and own the ANZ Operational Excellence strategy, translating business goals into a multi-year roadmap tailored to local market nuances.

• Design and maintain the Target Operating Model (TOM) to ensure clear accountability, escalation governance, and seamless hand-offs across Planning, Procurement, FSQA, and Fulfillment.

• Lead a portfolio of high-complexity projects using Lean, Six Sigma, or Kaizen methodologies to drive step-change improvements in Cost per Box (CPB), Cost of Goods Sold (COGS), and operational error rates.

• Identify E2E supply chain bottlenecks and standardize tools and systems to reduce manual intervention, enhance data integrity, and drive supply chain digitalization.

• Establish a robust project governance framework and analyze cross-functional performance data to prioritize high-leverage opportunities for waste reduction and cost optimization.

• Build a Continuous Improvement (CI) DNA across ANZ by designing training programs, coaching regional teams, and scaling best practices across our network.

• Act as the primary bridge for ANZ leadership to ensure operational consistency and alignment across all business units.

 

You have…

• Deep operational expertise across Supply Chain pillars (Planning, FSQA, Procurement, and Fulfillment) within high-growth, complex environments.

• Proven experience designing Target Operating Models and E2E frameworks, along with a track record of leading large-scale organizational change.

• Demonstrated mastery in project governance and continuous improvement methodologies (such as Lean, Six Sigma, or Kaizen) with a history of delivering measurable ROI.

• Strong analytical and technical judgement, with the ability to use data-driven insights to identify systemic issues and drive financial targets.

You are…

• A strategic, systems-level thinker who anticipates E2E supply chain impacts and moves proactively from reactive troubleshooting to systemic prevention.

• An influential communicator with high emotional intelligence, capable of pitching process improvements to the C-suite and running Kaizen events on the warehouse floor.

• Autonomous and results-oriented, bringing a "Founder’s Mentality" to navigate ambiguity and take full accountability for cross-functional KPIs without formal authority.

• A natural coach and mentor who leads by example, challenges the status quo, and elevates the problem-solving capabilities of peers and operational leads.

What you’ll get in return… 

 

• The chance to have a significant impact in a leading global food technology company

• Flexible working arrangements 

• Egoless environment, constant learning with room for personal growth

• Free access to Headspace

• Internal learning & development 

• A diverse and vibrant international environment, with offices in 18 countries

• Company discount - 70% off HelloFresh & 40% off Youfoodz

Start Date: Immediately available - Can wait a notice period

Duration: Permanent full time role

Location: Chippendale Head Office - hybrid working environment 

Salary: Competitive salary & employee benefits

title: Senior Product Designer, Global Payments
description:
ABOUT ZIP

Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement - built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before.

The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Zip’s team includes product leaders from Apple, Airbnb, and Meta, as well as former procurement leaders from United Health, Sanofi, MGM Resorts, Discover, and NASA.

Backed by Adams Street, Alkeon, BOND, CRV, DST, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator, Zip has raised $371 million, most recently at a $2.2 billion valuation and has been recognized by Forbes Fintech 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, Inc. Best in Business, and LinkedIn Top Startups.

YOUR ROLE

We're looking for a Senior Product Designer to own product design for our Global Payments team, the group that moves money for Zip's customers worldwide: over $30 billion in payouts and counting. The team is building Zip's next generation of payment rails, from direct bank integrations to new provider partnerships, and you'll own the product experience on top of them: how enterprises schedule, track, and trust payments at global scale. This role carries more product thinking than most design seats; you'll shape direction, not just execute it, and we're looking for someone who reads that as the draw. As the team's AI investments open up later this year, you'll shape those too. Please note, we are looking for someone who will be able to come into our San Francisco office on a hybrid basis (3 days / week).

YOU WILL

- Own the end-to-end payments experience: scheduling, tracking, and the failure and retry states where trust in money movement is won or lost.

- Shape product direction: frame the problem, write the brief when there isn't one, and drive decisions with evidence alongside engineering.

- Partner closely with engineers, and with PM and go-to-market stakeholders across P2P, to brainstorm, define, and implement new features and offerings.

- Design the experience layer of new payment rails as direct bank integrations and new providers come online, including how customers migrate without fear.

- Run your own research: get in front of customers through our SE, CS, and Sales partners, and test your work with the finance teams who move real money through these flows.

- Participate in regular design reviews with the broader design team.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 5+ years of experience designing complex B2B or workflow products; payments or fintech experience is a strong plus.

- Experience shipping at least one full product or significant feature end to end as the lead designer.

- Experience driving product decisions in ambiguous territory: you can frame a problem, align partners, and move without waiting for a spec.

- Experience running your own research: finding the right customers, asking the right questions, and turning what you hear into design decisions.

- Experience iterating closely with engineers on both UX and visual design to get the details just right.

- A point of view: you can defend design decisions with PMs and engineers, and change your mind when the evidence says you should.

- Fluency in Figma and prototyping tools.

- Understanding of the technical constraints of building web applications.

NICE TO HAVES

- You build with AI tools in your own workflow, prototyping with Claude, Figma Make, Cursor, or whatever gets your ideas into something clickable fastest.

- Experience designing for operations-heavy users: AP, treasury, or finance teams who live in these tools eight hours a day.
